subject.title: Plugin Hooks: Missing trace context for observability (messageId, runId in all hooks, parentSpanId)

question: Which stable Plugin SDK trace-correlation contract should OpenClaw expose across agent, message, and subagent hooks for observability plugins?
rationale: The remaining work is a public API and privacy-boundary choice across multiple hook families, so automation cannot safely choose field names, optionality, timing, or whether span aliases should duplicate DiagnosticTraceContext.

options.title: Approve coherent additive contract
options.body: Define a single backwards-compatible contract covering runId, message/sender identity, trace/span aliases, and subagent requester/child run IDs before implementation slices land.

options.title: Land a smaller runId slice
options.body: Thread outbound runId and requesterRunId first while deferring span alias and prompt/message identity semantics to narrower follow-up issues.

options.title: Keep trace under diagnostics only
options.body: Decline broader plugin-hook trace fields and direct observability plugins toward diagnostics events plus existing hook payloads.

recommendation.title: Approve coherent additive contract
recommendation.body: Define a single backwards-compatible contract covering runId, message/sender identity, trace/span aliases, and subagent requester/child run IDs before implementation slices land.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is tied to current local hook blame and merged the closest outbound and reply-hook contract slices, making them the best available owner for the API boundary choice.
